title: Emilia-Romagna Stays Under the National Average as Pump Prices Climb Four Days Running
dek: Self-service petrol and diesel in Emilia-Romagna are cheaper than the rest of Italy today, even as both fuels post their fourth straight daily rise.
body: Drivers filling up in Emilia-Romagna paid an average of €2.002 per litre for self-service Benzina and €2.116 for self-service Gasolio on August 15th — both a touch below the national self-service averages of €2.004 and €2.122. The gap is modest, roughly a quarter of a cent on petrol and just over half a cent on diesel, but it puts the region among the more affordable places in Italy to fill a tank right now.

That relative discount comes despite a clear local uptrend: after bottoming out on August 11th, both fuels have risen for four consecutive days, with Gasolio climbing nearly 1.7 cents and Benzina up close to 0.8 cents over that stretch. The region's 1,877 registered stations reported 1,729 active price updates today, a 92% reporting rate that edges out the national figure of roughly 90.5% across all 23,963 registered stations — a small but telling sign the local network is keeping pace with the rest of the country.

Tracking a single region's daily swings against the national picture, station by station, is the kind of detail that would be tedious to maintain by hand in a spreadsheet. Fuel Dashboard does it automatically: every region takes its turn in a daily rotation, the numbers are pulled fresh from MIMIT each morning, and the whole site rebuilds itself without anyone touching a formula — built with Claude Code.
